full_prompt: A talking-portrait sprite sheet for a game's dialogue: one character, a smug cartoon rock-star mech pilot: big swoopy black pompadour, star-shaped red sunglasses pushed up on his forehead, stubble, leather jacket with a guitar pin, cocky grin, chunky outlines, drawn 16 times in a grid of 4 columns and 4 rows of equal square cells, with clear gaps of flat background between the cells so no two portraits touch. Every cell is the same head-and-shoulders bust facing the viewer, centered in its cell, at exactly the same position, size, pose, framing, lighting and colors, the shoulders cut off by a straight horizontal line near the bottom of the cell. Keep the character identical in every cell (same face shape, hair, clothes, accessories, proportions and outline): it is one drawing whose mouth, eyes and eyebrows are redrawn, and nothing else moves. Columns are mouth shapes for lip-sync, left to right: 1 mouth closed, 2 mouth slightly open, 3 mouth open, 4 mouth wide open as if shouting. Rows are expressions, top to bottom: row 1 neutral; row 2 smug; row 3 angry; row 4 the neutral face with both eyes fully closed (a blink), the mouth still changing across the columns. Nothing else in the image. Pixel art: big crisp square pixels as if each cell were drawn on a 48×48 grid, no anti-aliasing, no dithering noise, a limited palette. Background: one flat, solid pure blue color (#0000ff) filling everything behind the subject: no gradient, no texture, no shadow, no glow. Don't use that color anywhere in the subject. Avoid: text, letters, watermark, signature, logo, frame or border. An original design: not any existing character, franchise, brand or logo.
